note: Teaching text, clarifying questions, inferred constraints and own examples. Inferred, not official. Examples are small generated inputs with outputs from the independent references in oracles.py.

clarifyingQuestions: In which order should the community ids be returned?
Can the two lists disagree with each other?
What does the second part change: are chains of shared followers counted?
Can communityIdx be negative?
hints: Two communities are related when some follower follows both: start from the followers of communityIdx.
For each such follower, followerToCommunities lists every community it follows; mark those.
Unmark communityIdx itself and emit marked indices in increasing order, parsing the number after "C" and "F".
invariants: a community appears at most once in the result
communityIdx never appears in the result
chooseWhen: Bipartite membership data where a two-step neighbourhood is needed
tradeoffs: Marking by index needs O(n) memory; a hash set is smaller when results are sparse but needs a sort

clarifyingQuestions: In which order should the community ids be returned?
Can the two lists disagree with each other?
What does the second part change: are chains of shared followers counted?
Can communityIdx be negative?
hints: Treat communities and followers as the two sides of one graph.
A breadth-first search from communityIdx alternates community -> follower -> community.
Mark visited followers too, so each membership is examined once; report visited communities except the start in index order.
invariants: each community and follower is enqueued at most once
the result is closed under shared followers
chooseWhen: Connected components in bipartite membership data
tradeoffs: A union-find over all memberships answers many queries at once; one BFS is simpler for a single query
hack2hire:69557dad4a0202df9569e983.variantLabel: Inferred level 2: communities connected through chains of shared followers

clarifyingQuestions: What is returned: the remaining intervals, the removed value, or the new flattened list?
Are the input intervals sorted?
What happens when idx is past the last covered point?
Should an emptied interval be kept?
hints: Each interval [s, e) contributes e - s points to the flattened sequence.
Skip whole intervals while idx is at least their length, subtracting it.
The point is p = s + idx inside the interval reached; emit [s, p) and [p + 1, e) when non-empty and copy every other interval.
invariants: total covered points decrease by exactly one when idx is in range
output intervals stay non-overlapping
chooseWhen: Index arithmetic over run-length encoded ranges
tradeoffs: A prefix-sum array plus binary search helps for many removals; a single removal needs one linear pass
hack2hire:684dee4b5e4cf21833c0611f.variantLabel: Inferred single variant: remove the idx-th covered point and return remaining intervals

clarifyingQuestions: Is y a vowel?
Are one-letter words like "a" changed?
May words contain digits or punctuation?
Should the input array be modified in place?
hints: Check text[i][0] and text[i][-1] against the vowel set in lowercase.
Only the characters strictly between the first and last positions move.
Swap from both ends toward the middle (or reverse the middle slice), leaving the ends in place.
invariants: word lengths are preserved
non-qualifying words are returned unchanged
chooseWhen: Per-token string transforms
tradeoffs: Building new strings costs O(length) per word; in-place swaps need a mutable character array
hack2hire:69a32b466e73e4abccc9bf13.variantLabel: Inferred single variant: reverse the middle of words that start and end with a vowel

constraints: allowed[i] and disallowed[i] each hold at most 10 distinct names
clarifyingQuestions: Does a disallow on a role override privileges it inherits?
Does a child inherit what a parent explicitly disallows from its own parents?
Can a role allow and disallow the same privilege?
In what order are roles and privileges returned?
hints: A role depends only on its parents, so roles must be processed after all their parents: a topological order.
Count unprocessed parents per role and start with roles that have none (Kahn's algorithm), avoiding recursion on deep chains.
For each role take the union of its allowed list and its parents' final sets, remove its disallowed list, then sort for output.
invariants: a role is computed only after all its parents
no privilege in disallowed[i] appears in the final set of roles[i]
chooseWhen: Inherited configuration over a DAG
tradeoffs: Materialising full sets per role costs O(n P) memory; bitsets shrink this when privileges are few
hack2hire:6801c3b66cd5d6c88778f20c.variantLabel: Inferred single variant: final privileges through inheritance with disallow overrides

constraints: consecutive waypoints distinct with integer segment length
clarifyingQuestions: What is returned per distance: a distance value, a waypoint index or a coordinate?
Is nearness measured to every waypoint or only the current segment ends?
What happens past the end of the route?
How are ties broken?
hints: Prefix sums of segment lengths tell which segment a distance d falls on.
On segment A -> B of length L, the position is A + (r / L)(B - A) with r = d minus the prefix; multiply through by L to stay in integers.
Compare (L(Ax - Wx) + r(Bx - Ax))^2 + (L(Ay - Wy) + r(By - Ay))^2 over waypoints W: the common factor L^2 does not change the order.
invariants: positions are monotone along the route in d
all comparisons are exact integer comparisons
chooseWhen: Geometry where exact arithmetic avoids floating-point ties
tradeoffs: Scanning all waypoints per query is O(N Q); a spatial index helps only for much larger inputs
hack2hire:69cae7e2ff3ebde766ceda54.variantLabel: Inferred single variant: nearest waypoint index at each travelled distance

constraints: trees may be as deep as their node count
clarifyingQuestions: Is the question whether the visible text is identical, or whether the structure is identical?
Can text be split differently across labels and still match?
Can grouping labels carry text?
How deep can the trees be?
hints: Only leaf texts in pre-order matter, so the structure can differ between the trees.
An explicit stack of node indices gives the next leaf without recursion, so deep trees are safe.
Keep a position inside the current leaf of each tree and compare one character at a time; both sides must run out together.
invariants: each node is pushed at most once per tree
characters are compared in word order
chooseWhen: Comparing streams produced by two different tree shapes
tradeoffs: Lazy comparison stops at the first mismatch; building both strings is simpler but always pays O(word length)
hack2hire:68aebce1c8631a6568126eb4.variantLabel: Inferred single variant: equal concatenated leaf text of two label trees

clarifyingQuestions: Which eligible plane receives an item: earliest departure, best fit or largest capacity?
Are items placed in the given order or sorted?
What is returned for a rejected order?
Are orders processed in input order or by ship time?
hints: Sort planes by departure; the eligible planes for an order form a suffix found by binary search.
The first plane in that suffix with remaining capacity >= size can be found with a max segment tree by descending into the leftmost child that is large enough.
Record each capacity change during an order and undo them in reverse when an item fails.
invariants: capacities never go negative
a rejected order leaves every capacity unchanged
chooseWhen: First-fit allocation over an ordered resource list
tradeoffs: A segment tree makes each placement logarithmic; a linear scan is simpler and fine for small fleets
hack2hire:69752cb217272b5c868d5e84.variantLabel: Inferred single variant: earliest-departure first fit with all-or-nothing orders

clarifyingQuestions: Does a repeated search move the term to the front?
Does getTopK count as a use for eviction?
In which order are top k terms returned?
What if k exceeds the number of stored terms?
hints: A hash map finds a term in O(1); a doubly linked list keeps recency order with O(1) moves.
Use head and tail sentinel nodes so insertion and removal never special-case the ends.
On overflow remove the node before the tail sentinel and delete its key; getTopK follows next pointers from the head.
invariants: map size equals list length and never exceeds capacity
list order is strictly by last add
chooseWhen: LRU caches that also need ordered reads of the newest entries
tradeoffs: A linked list costs extra pointers per entry; an insertion-ordered map can replace it when only the oldest entry must be found
hack2hire:678879df402dc47b67a14946.variantLabel: Inferred single variant: LRU search history with most-recent-first top k

clarifyingQuestions: Is the input always one valid chain?
What is returned when segments form a cycle or several chains?
Can a segment start and end at the same id?
May payloads be empty?
hints: The chain head is the one segment whose startId is not any segment's endId.
Index segments by startId so the successor of a segment is a single lookup of its endId.
Collect payloads in a list and join once at the end to avoid quadratic string building.
invariants: each segment is visited once
the walk ends at the only end that is not a start
chooseWhen: Reassembling ordered fragments keyed by their boundaries
tradeoffs: A hash map costs O(n) memory; sorting by keys cannot recover chain order
hack2hire:6a4809cfca956256d786d255.variantLabel: Inferred level 1: reconstruct one valid chain

clarifyingQuestions: Is the input always one valid chain?
What is returned when segments form a cycle or several chains?
Can a segment start and end at the same id?
May payloads be empty?
hints: With unique starts and unique ends, segments form disjoint paths and cycles.
A single chain has exactly one head (a start that is not an end) and a walk from it visits every segment.
Count heads first; then walk and compare the number of visited segments with n.
invariants: valid input has exactly one head
a cycle has no head
chooseWhen: Validating linked structures given as unordered records
tradeoffs: Checking the visit count is cheaper than detecting cycles explicitly
hack2hire:6a480ba0ca956256d786d277.variantLabel: Inferred level 2: reconstruct or reject an unvalidated chain

clarifyingQuestions: Is the input always one valid chain?
What is returned when segments form a cycle or several chains?
Can a segment start and end at the same id?
May payloads be empty?
hints: Every chain has exactly one head: a startId that is no segment's endId.
Sort the heads by id to fix the output order.
Walk each chain through a startId map; every segment belongs to exactly one chain.
invariants: each segment is visited exactly once over all walks
the number of outputs equals the number of heads
chooseWhen: Reassembling several independent fragment streams
tradeoffs: Sorting heads costs O(h log h); walking order is otherwise linear
hack2hire:6a480bbbca956256d786d279.variantLabel: Inferred level 3: reconstruct several disjoint chains

constraints: at most 1000 variations per sentence and 5e4 in total
clarifyingQuestions: Should the answer list the sentences or only count them?
Is the original word always allowed even when it is not in wordSet?
In what order should variations be returned?
Can a sentence contain the same word twice?
hints: Anagrams share a signature: the word with its letters sorted.
Group wordSet by signature once; each sentence word then has a sorted option list (its group plus itself).
Expand the product left to right; equal-length options keep the joined strings in sorted order without a final sort.
invariants: every variation has the same word lengths as the original sentence
the number of variations is the product of option counts
chooseWhen: Enumerating combinations of interchangeable tokens
tradeoffs: Output size can be exponential in sentence length; counting alone would only need the product
hack2hire:699bb05f6e73e4abccc9a9e4.variantLabel: Inferred single variant: all anagram substitutions of each sentence

clarifyingQuestions: Which shard gives way when too many overlap: the later one, the longer one?
Is a shard trimmed at its start, its end, or split?
How are gaps filled, and by which shard?
Are fully covered shards removed?
In which order are shards returned?
hints: Process shards by start: then only already kept shards constrain the current one.
With this order the kept coverage is non-increasing from the current start onward, so the keys still over the limit form a prefix of the shard.
Binary search the first point where coverage drops below the limit, using sorted starts and ends; afterwards walk kept shards by start and pull each start back to close a gap.
invariants: no key is covered by more than limit kept shards
kept ranges only shrink before the gap fill, which only extends starts backward
chooseWhen: Interval capacity enforcement with a deterministic tie order
tradeoffs: Sorted-array insertion is O(n) per shard; a balanced tree or Fenwick tree over compressed keys removes that cost
hack2hire:69a3c6546e73e4abccc9c150.variantLabel: Inferred single variant: trim shards to a coverage limit, then fill gaps

clarifyingQuestions: What is maximised: protected population or number of protected cities?
Can a unit move more than once or to the right?
Can two units protect the same city?
Is the unit at city 0 able to move?
hints: A unit can only reach its own city or the one to its left, so runs of consecutive units act independently.
A run of L units starting at s can cover L of the cities s - 1 .. s + L - 1: units left of the skipped city move left, the others stay.
For each run skip the least populated of those L + 1 cities; a run starting at city 0 has no city to its left and covers itself.
invariants: each run is handled once
the answer never exceeds the total population
chooseWhen: Assignment problems on a line with one-step moves
tradeoffs: The run argument is O(n) and exact; a two-state DP generalises to other costs
hack2hire:6a32d45b65569fa70cc7eb97.variantLabel: Inferred single variant: maximise protected population with one-step left moves

clarifyingQuestions: Are routes directed?
How many transfers may a path use in each part?
How are paths and costs reported, and in what order?
What is returned when no path exists?
hints: Split each route on ":" into four fields and convert the cost to an integer.
Keep routes whose source and target match.
Sort by cost, then by method name.
invariants: each matching route appears once
output costs are non-decreasing
chooseWhen: Parsing and filtering delimited records
tradeoffs: Parsing all routes is O(R) even for one query; an index pays off for many queries
hack2hire:6976850c5ed12b33b05f0f0f.variantLabel: Inferred level 1: direct routes between two countries

clarifyingQuestions: Are routes directed?
How many transfers may a path use in each part?
How are paths and costs reported, and in what order?
What is returned when no path exists?
hints: Group routes by source country.
Direct routes source -> target are paths; a route source -> X followed by X -> target is a path when X is neither endpoint.
Build path strings with ":" and sort by (cost, path).
invariants: no path revisits source or target
total cost is the sum of its route costs

tradeoffs: Enumeration size is the product of degrees; only small hop limits stay tractable
hack2hire:697690985ed12b33b05f0f2c.variantLabel: Inferred level 2: paths with at most one transfer

clarifyingQuestions: Are routes directed?
How many transfers may a path use in each part?
How are paths and costs reported, and in what order?
What is returned when no path exists?
hints: Costs are positive, so the cheapest path never repeats a country.
Several methods between the same countries only matter through their cheapest one.
Run Dijkstra from source with a binary heap and stop when target is popped.
invariants: popped distances are final
distances are sums of positive integers below 2**53

tradeoffs: Dijkstra is O(R log R); Bellman-Ford is simpler but O(V R)
hack2hire:697692bb5ed12b33b05f0f34.variantLabel: Inferred level 3: cheapest path with any number of transfers

constraints: exactly one S and one D
clarifyingQuestions: Does entering a station refill to full or add a fixed amount?
What is returned when D is unreachable?
Can you pass through D or S again?
Does reaching D with zero fuel count?
hints: The state is the cell together with remaining fuel; plain BFS on cells alone is wrong.
BFS explores states by move count, so a later state at a cell is useful only if it carries more fuel than every earlier one.
Track the best fuel per cell and skip dominated states; refill on G before expanding.
invariants: move counts are non-decreasing in BFS order
a pruned state is dominated by an earlier state with at least as much fuel
chooseWhen: Shortest paths with a resource that resets
tradeoffs: Dominance pruning keeps typical searches near O(m n); the worst case is still O(m n F)
hack2hire:68dc5856dd5418be11109afb.variantLabel: Inferred single variant: fewest moves with fuel limit and refuelling stations

clarifyingQuestions: How is a matrix passed in and returned: dense lists or sparse triples?
Do add and multiply modify the stored matrix?
Which other operations are needed?
Should zero results be stored or reported?
hints: Store only non-zero entries, keyed by row then column.
For multiplication, a non-zero A[i][k] only meets the non-zeros of row k of the operand.
Delete entries that become zero so the store stays minimal, and sort row and column keys when emitting triples.
invariants: the store never holds a zero value
operations return fresh lists and leave the operand unchanged
chooseWhen: Linear algebra on mostly-zero data
tradeoffs: Hash maps per row cost more per entry than CSR arrays but allow O(1) updates
hack2hire:690d00010a0bc710235894c4.variantLabel: Inferred single variant: sparse matrix class with get, set, add and multiply

Which index is returned if several exist?
Can values be zero or negative?

Walk left to right keeping the prefix sum through index i.
Return i when 2 * prefix equals the total; stop early once the prefix exceeds half.
invariants: the prefix sum strictly increases
sums stay below 2**53
